projects.description: launched a community-led clean water project to address declining water quality in local streams and wells caused by soil erosion, agricultural runoff, and inadequate sanitation infrastructure. For years, families relied on untreated surface water for household use, increasing health risks and limiting productivity. Recognizing the connection between environmental stewardship and community well-being, farmers came together to design a sustainable solution that would protect their shared water sources while strengthening agricultural resilience. The project focused on restoring watershed health and improving access to safe drinking water. Farmers established vegetative buffer zones along riverbanks to reduce runoff, planted native trees to stabilize soil, and adopted soil conservation practices such as cover cropping and reduced tillage. In parallel, the community installed a gravity-fed water filtration system and constructed protected spring catchments to ensure clean, reliable water

projects.description: The Tutaekuri-Waimate Stream Restoration and Protection Project aims to restore and protect the Waimate Stream along Chesterhope Station, which was severely impacted by Cyclone Gabrielle. The project involves fencing off stream edges and planting native vegetation to exclude livestock, stabilize banks, improve water quality, and enhance biodiversity. Initial work has already seen 700 meters fenced and planted in July 2025. This is a collaboration between the Joan Fernie Charitable Trust (JFCT) and Fair Trade, with plans to extend restoration along the entire stream boundary. Completion will involve continued planting, fencing, and monitoring with support from trustees and local volunteers.
projects.name: 2025 D2 Waimate Stream Restoration Project
projects.primaryGoal: The project will: Exclude livestock from the stream to prevent contamination. Stabilize stream banks and reduce erosion. Improve water quality and restore natural habitats. Promote biodiversity and resilience against future weather events. Impact will be measured by: Length of stream fenced and planted. Survival rates of native plants. Water quality improvements and biodiversity indicators. Beneficiaries include local communities, environmental stakeholders, and future generations who rely on a healthy ecosystem.
